s601.content:
According to tradition, Sophia was a Christian widow in Rome whose three young daughters, named Faith, Hope, and Charity (Pistis, Elpis, and Agape), were martyred in front of her under the emperor Hadrian.

Sophia buried them and died of grief at their grave a few days later. They are especially beloved in the Slavic lands, where Vera, Nadezhda, and Lyubov are common names in their honor.
s601.intercession: Sts. Sophia, Faith, Hope, and Charity, pray for us. Strengthen mothers who suffer, and give us faith, hope, and love. Amen.

s602.content:
Irene was a noblewoman from Cappadocia who, according to her Life, came to Constantinople as a possible bride for the emperor. Instead she entered the Monastery of Chrysovalantou and became its abbess.

She was known for long vigils of prayer, wise discernment, and care for her sisters, and many sought her prayers. She is greatly loved in Greece.
s602.intercession: St. Irene, pray for us. Teach us to watch and pray. Amen.

s603.content:
Febronia was a young nun of Nisibis in Mesopotamia, raised in a convent from childhood and known for her learning and holiness. During the persecution of Diocletian she was arrested.

She refused to renounce Christ and to accept marriage to a pagan official, and she was tortured and killed. Her Life, said to be written by a sister of her convent, made her one of the most honored martyrs of the Syriac and Byzantine Churches.
s603.intercession: St. Febronia, pray for us. Give us steadfast faith in time of trial. Amen.

s604.content:
Zosimas was a monk and priest in Palestine. According to the Life written by St. Sophronius of Jerusalem, during a Lenten retreat in the desert beyond the Jordan he met St. Mary of Egypt, who told him the story of her conversion.

The next year he brought her Holy Communion, and a year later he found her body and buried it. The Byzantine Churches read her story during the Great Fast.
s604.intercession: St. Zosimas, pray for us. Make us humble enough to learn from every soul God sends us. Amen.

s605.content:
Philaret was a wealthy landowner of Paphlagonia, in present-day Turkey, who gave so generously to the poor that he gave away nearly everything he owned, trusting that God would provide.

According to his Life, his granddaughter Maria was chosen as the bride of the emperor Constantine VI, and his family’s fortunes were restored. He continued to give alms until his death.
s605.intercession: St. Philaret, pray for us. Make us generous to the poor. Amen.

s606.content:
Drogo was a Flemish nobleman who, as a young man, gave away his inheritance and became a penitent pilgrim, traveling to Rome many times. He later worked as a shepherd.

After an illness left him badly disfigured, he lived for decades as a recluse in a small cell built against the church at Sebourg, receiving Holy Communion through a window and living on very little. He is the patron of shepherds, of coffee house owners, and of those who are mocked for their appearance.
s606.intercession: St. Drogo, pray for us. Help us to see beyond appearances to the beauty of every soul. Amen.

s607.content:
Notburga was a peasant girl of the Tyrol who worked as a kitchen maid and later as a farm servant. She gave her own food to the poor, and when her employer forbade it, she was dismissed for a time.

According to a well-known story, when a farmer ordered her to keep working on a Saturday evening after the bell for Sunday had rung, she threw her sickle into the air and it hung there. She is the patron of servants, farm workers, and the Tyrol.
s607.intercession: St. Notburga, pray for us. Bless all who work hard for others, and help us keep the Lord’s Day holy. Amen.

s608.content:
According to tradition, Eustace was a Roman general named Placidus. While hunting, he saw a stag with a crucifix shining between its antlers and heard Christ calling him. He was baptized with his wife and sons.

He lost his wealth and his family was scattered, but they were reunited, and under Hadrian they were martyred together for refusing to sacrifice to idols. He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers and the patron of hunters and of all who face adversity.
s608.intercession: St. Eustace, pray for us. Help us to stay faithful when trials come. Amen.

s609.content:
Honoratus (Honoré) was a bishop of Amiens in northern France. A legend tells that when news of his election reached his old nurse, she said she would believe it when the baker’s peel in her hand took root, and it grew into a mulberry tree.

He is the patron of bakers and pastry chefs. The Rue Saint-Honoré in Paris and the Saint-Honoré cake are named after him.
s609.intercession: St. Honoratus, pray for us. Bless all who make our daily bread. Amen.

s610.content:
Lydia was a businesswoman from Thyatira who sold purple cloth in the city of Philippi. When St. Paul preached by the riverside, the Lord opened her heart to his message, and she and her household were baptized (Acts 16).

She was the first recorded convert in Europe, and she welcomed Paul and his companions into her home, which became a meeting place for the young church. She is the patron of dyers and of businesswomen.
s610.intercession: St. Lydia, pray for us. Open our hearts to the Word of God and our homes to others. Amen.

s611.content:
Fabiola was a wealthy Roman noblewoman who divorced a cruel and abusive husband and remarried. After her second husband died, she did public penance before the Church at the Lateran Basilica.

She used her fortune to found what is often called the first public hospital in Rome, where she cared for the sick herself. St. Jerome, her friend, wrote of her generosity. She is the patron of the divorced, of difficult marriages, and of victims of abuse.
s611.intercession: St. Fabiola, pray for us. Heal the wounded, and give new beginnings to those whose marriages have suffered. Amen.

s612.content:
Medard was a bishop of Noyon and Tournai in Gaul, known for his kindness to the poor. A legend says that as a boy he was sheltered from a rainstorm by an eagle hovering over his head.

He is invoked for good weather and is the patron of farmers and vineyards. An old French proverb says that if it rains on St. Medard’s Day, it will rain for forty days.
s612.intercession: St. Medard, pray for us. Bless our crops and our harvests. Amen.

s613.content:
Dorothy was a young Christian of Caesarea in Cappadocia, martyred during the persecution of Diocletian. A famous legend says that as she was led to execution, a lawyer named Theophilus mocked her, asking her to send him fruit from the garden of paradise.

After her death, a child brought him a basket of roses and apples, and he was converted and later martyred himself. She is the patron of gardeners, florists, and brides.
s613.intercession: St. Dorothy, pray for us. Let our lives bear flowers and fruit for heaven. Amen.

s614.content:
Gummarus (Gommaire) was a courtier in the service of Pepin the Short. He married a noblewoman who proved harsh and quarrelsome, especially toward their servants, and he bore it with great patience, quietly making amends to those she wronged.

In later life he lived as a hermit, and the town of Lier in Belgium grew up around his hermitage. He is the patron of difficult marriages and separated spouses.
s614.intercession: St. Gummarus, pray for us. Give patience and peace to those in difficult marriages. Amen.

s615.content:
Adrian was a pagan officer at Nicomedia. While overseeing the torture of Christians, he was so moved by their courage that he declared himself a Christian and was imprisoned with them.

His wife Natalia, a secret Christian, encouraged him in prison and stayed with him as he was martyred. She later died in peace and is honored with him as a martyr. He is a patron of soldiers, butchers, and guards.
s615.intercession: Sts. Adrian and Natalia, pray for us. Help husbands and wives to lead each other to heaven. Amen.

s616.content:
Ubald Baldassini was bishop of Gubbio in Umbria, a gentle and patient pastor who reformed his clergy and made peace among quarreling citizens.

In 1155, when the army of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa threatened Gubbio, Ubald went out to meet the emperor and persuaded him to spare the city. Gubbio still honors him every May 15 with the famous Festa dei Ceri. He is the patron of Gubbio.
s616.intercession: St. Ubald, pray for us. Make us peacemakers in our homes and cities. Amen.

s617.content:
Emygdius was a bishop of Ascoli Piceno in central Italy, martyred during the persecution of Diocletian.

When a great earthquake struck the region in 1703 and Ascoli was spared, the people credited his prayers. Since then he has been invoked as a protector against earthquakes, and many cities in earthquake zones have placed themselves under his patronage.
s617.intercession: St. Emygdius, pray for us. Protect us from earthquakes and every disaster. Amen.

s618.content:
Bavo was a wealthy and worldly nobleman in what is now Belgium. After the death of his wife, he was converted by the preaching of St. Amand, gave away his riches to the poor, and entered the monastery at Ghent.

He later lived as a hermit in great penance. He is the patron of Ghent and Haarlem, whose cathedrals bear his name.
s618.intercession: St. Bavo, pray for us. Help us turn away from worldly things to the love of God. Amen.

s619.content:
Odile was born blind to an Alsatian duke who rejected her because of it. She was raised in a convent, and tradition says she received her sight when she was baptized.

She later reconciled with her father and founded an abbey on a mountain in the Vosges, now called Mont Sainte-Odile, and a hospice for the sick and the poor below it. She is the patron of Alsace and of the blind.
s619.intercession: St. Odile, pray for us. Give light to our eyes and to our souls. Amen.

s620.content:
Oswald was a prince of Northumbria who, in exile, was baptized by the monks of Iona. When he returned to claim his kingdom, he set up a wooden cross before the battle of Heavenfield and prayed with his army before winning the victory.

As king he invited St. Aidan to evangelize his people and sometimes translated Aidan’s sermons himself. He was killed in battle against the pagan King Penda in 642 and was venerated as a martyr.
s620.intercession: St. Oswald, pray for us. Make us bold to raise the cross of Christ. Amen.

s621.content:
Wiborada was a Swabian noblewoman who lived as an anchoress, walled into a cell next to a church at St. Gallen, giving counsel through a window.

She foresaw the attack of Hungarian raiders in 926 and warned the monks of St. Gall, who hid their books and escaped. She refused to leave her cell and was killed. In 1047 she became the first woman formally canonized by a pope. She is the patron of libraries and librarians.
s621.intercession: St. Wiborada, pray for us. Protect books, libraries, and all who love learning. Amen.

s622.content:
Benno was bishop of Meissen in Saxony during the conflict between Pope Gregory VII and Emperor Henry IV, and he suffered imprisonment and exile for siding with the pope.

A legend says that before going into exile he threw the keys of his cathedral into the Elbe, and on his return they were found in a fish. His relics rest in Munich, and he is the patron of Munich and of fishermen.
s622.intercession: St. Benno, pray for us. Keep us faithful to the Church in times of conflict. Amen.

s623.content:
Goar was a priest from Aquitaine who settled as a hermit on the banks of the Rhine, where travelers and boatmen faced a dangerous stretch of river.

He welcomed everyone into his home, fed them, and cared for them. The town of St. Goar grew up at the site. He is the patron of innkeepers, potters, and boatmen.
s623.intercession: St. Goar, pray for us. Make us generous in welcoming others. Amen.

s624.content:
Gertrude was the daughter of the Frankish nobleman Pepin of Landen and St. Itta. Refusing marriage, she became abbess of the monastery her mother founded at Nivelles, in present-day Belgium, when she was about twenty.

She gave hospitality to pilgrims and Irish missionary monks and was devoted to study of the Scriptures. She is the patron of travelers and gardeners, and in modern times she has been called the patron of cats.
s624.intercession: St. Gertrude, pray for us. Bless all travelers and give them a safe welcome. Amen.

s626.content:
Benedict was born near Messina in Sicily to parents who had been brought from Africa as slaves. Freed as a young man, he endured ridicule for his color, joined a community of hermits, and later became a Franciscan lay brother in Palermo, where he worked as a cook.

Though he could not read, his wisdom was so great that he was elected superior of the friary. He was canonized in 1807 and is a patron of Palermo and of African Americans.
s626.intercession: St. Benedict the Moor, pray for us. Heal the wounds of racism and help us see Christ in one another. Amen.

s627.content:
Bona was a young woman of Pisa who, from childhood, longed to visit the holy places. She made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem, where she was captured by pirates and later ransomed, and she went on to make many pilgrimages to Rome and to Santiago de Compostela.

She became a guide for other pilgrims on the long and dangerous road. In 1962 Pope St. John XXIII named her patron of flight attendants. She is also a patron of travelers and of Pisa.
s627.intercession: St. Bona, pray for us. Protect all who travel, and keep our hearts on the road to heaven. Amen.

s628.content:
St. Julian is known only from a medieval legend. It tells of a nobleman who, through a terrible mistake, killed his own parents. In penance he and his wife built a hospice beside a river, where he ferried travelers across and cared for the poor and the sick.

One night he gave his own bed to a leper, who revealed himself as Christ and told him he was forgiven. He is the patron of innkeepers, ferrymen, and travelers.
s628.intercession: St. Julian, pray for us. Help us to welcome Christ in every guest. Amen.

s629.content:
Expeditus is listed among martyrs of Melitene in Armenia, but almost nothing is known of his life. A popular story tells that when he decided to become a Christian, the devil appeared as a crow crying "cras," Latin for "tomorrow." Expeditus stamped on it and said "hodie," "today."

He is popularly invoked in urgent needs and by those tempted to put off conversion or their duties.
s629.intercession: St. Expeditus, pray for us. Help us not to put off until tomorrow what God asks of us today. Amen.

s630.content:
Christina was an orphaned peasant girl of Brustem, near Liège. Her Life, written soon after her death by the Dominican Thomas of Cantimpré, tells that at about twenty-one she suffered a seizure and was thought dead, but during her funeral Mass she rose from the coffin and fled to the rafters of the church.

She said she had been shown purgatory, and she spent the rest of her life in extraordinary penances offered for the souls there. Many thought her mad. She is the patron of those with mental illness and of those who care for them.
s630.intercession: St. Christina, pray for us. Comfort all who suffer in mind, and pray for the souls in purgatory. Amen.

s631.content:
Godelieve was a gentle young Flemish noblewoman married to a nobleman named Bertolf of Gistel. Her husband and his mother turned against her, mistreated her, and kept her half-starved, but she answered with patience and prayer.

At about twenty-one she was strangled on her husband’s orders. She is the patron of difficult marriages and of victims of abuse, and pilgrims still visit the abbey at Gistel that bears her name.
s631.intercession: St. Godelieve, pray for us. Protect all who suffer in their own homes. Amen.

s632.content:
Margaret was born to a noble family in Umbria, blind, with a curved spine, a shortened leg, and very small stature. Ashamed of her, her parents kept her hidden and walled up for years, then abandoned her at a shrine in Città di Castello.

Taken in by poor families, she became a Dominican tertiary known for her cheerfulness, her prayer, and her care for children and prisoners. Pope Francis canonized her in 2021. She is the patron of the disabled and of the unwanted.
s632.intercession: St. Margaret of Castello, pray for us. Help us to welcome every life as a gift from God. Amen.

s633.content:
Amand was a monk from Aquitaine who became a missionary bishop in Flanders and the lands along the Scheldt, where Christianity had barely taken root. He was often mocked and driven away, but he kept preaching, ransomed captives, and founded monasteries, including the abbey at Elnone that later bore his name.

Because the regions he evangelized became famous for their vineyards and breweries, he is the patron of winemakers, brewers, and innkeepers.
s633.intercession: St. Amand, pray for us. Give us perseverance in sharing the faith. Amen.

s634.content:
Arnold was a soldier who became a Benedictine monk and later, against his wishes, bishop of Soissons in France. He worked to make peace among feuding nobles and founded an abbey in Flanders.

A well-known story says that during an epidemic he urged people to drink beer, made by boiling water, rather than water from the wells, and many were spared. He is a patron of brewers and hop pickers.
s634.intercession: St. Arnold, pray for us. Bless all who work to make peace. Amen.

s635.content:
Adjutor was a Norman knight who went on the First Crusade and, according to tradition, was captured and held prisoner before escaping and returning home.

He spent the rest of his life as a hermit near Vernon on the Seine. Stories of his rescues on the water made him the patron of swimmers, boaters, and those in danger of drowning.
s635.intercession: St. Adjutor, pray for us. Protect all who are on or in the water. Amen.

s636.content:
Peter González was a Spanish cathedral canon who lived a worldly life until a humiliating fall from his horse turned him to God. He became a Dominican friar and served as a chaplain to King St. Ferdinand III.

He spent his last years preaching to the sailors and fishermen of Galicia, who called him San Telmo. He is a patron of sailors, and "St. Elmo’s fire," the glow seen on ships’ masts in storms, is often linked with his name.
s636.intercession: St. Peter González, pray for us. Guide all sailors safely home. Amen.

s637.content:
Anna Francesca Boscardin was a slow, simple peasant girl, often called "the goose." She joined the Sisters of St. Dorothy at Vicenza and worked in the kitchen and laundry before becoming a nurse at the hospital in Treviso.

During the First World War she stayed with patients who could not be moved during air raids. She died at thirty-four and was canonized in 1961. She is loved as a patron of nurses.
s637.intercession: St. Maria Bertilla, pray for us. Make us faithful in small things and gentle with the sick. Amen.

s638.content:
Agostina was a farmer’s daughter who joined the Sisters of Charity of St. Jeanne-Antide Thouret and served as a nurse at the Hospital of the Holy Spirit in Rome, in the tuberculosis ward.

She cared lovingly for a violent patient who had threatened her, and in 1894 he stabbed her to death. She died forgiving him. She was canonized in 1999 and is a patron of nurses in Italy.
s638.intercession: St. Agostina, pray for us. Give nurses courage and love. Amen.

s639.content:
Erminio Pampuri was a young doctor who served as a medic in the First World War and then as a country physician near Milan, treating the poor for free and leading the young people of his parish.

In 1927 he joined the Hospitaller Brothers of St. John of God, taking the name Riccardo, and directed a clinic until he died of tuberculosis at thirty-three. He was canonized in 1989.
s639.intercession: St. Riccardo, pray for us. Bless all physicians and those they serve. Amen.

s640.content:
Ezequiél Moreno was a Spanish Augustinian Recollect who served as a missionary in the Philippines and later in Colombia, where he became bishop of Pasto.

He was a tireless pastor and preacher. He developed cancer of the nose and palate and bore great suffering before he died in Spain in 1906. He was canonized in 1992 and is the patron of cancer patients.
s640.intercession: St. Ezequiél, pray for us. Strengthen all who suffer from cancer. Amen.

s641.content:
Charles Houben was a Dutch Passionist priest who spent most of his life at Mount Argus in Dublin. He was a poor preacher, but his simple holiness and his blessings drew crowds from all over Ireland and England, and many healings were reported.

He was canonized in 2007. He is invoked by the sick.
s641.intercession: St. Charles, pray for us. Bless the sick and all who care for them. Amen.
